ai.literal: The means, and the time, and the manner of execution, and the difficult task to be performed, that which is excellent in these is the minister.
ai.translation: An excellent minister is one who excels in choosing the right means, the right time, the proper manner of execution, and the difficult task to be performed.
ai.modern: தேவையான கருவி, ஏற்ற காலம், செய்யும் முறை, செய்ய வேண்டிய அரிய செயல் ஆகியவற்றைச் சிறந்த முறையில் தேர்ந்தெடுப்பதே அமைச்சின் தன்மையாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the core responsibilities and qualities of a minister or ministry. A successful minister must possess excellence in four distinct areas: identifying the proper resources or instruments (karuvi), choosing the opportune moment (kālam), determining the correct method of execution (ceykai), and selecting the rare or difficult task (aruvinai) that needs to be accomplished. The word 'māṇṭatu' emphasizes that the ministry must be outstanding and glorious in managing these four elements. Thus, effective statecraft is presented as a masterful coordination of resources, timing, execution, and strategic goals.

ai.literal: Firmness of mind, protecting subjects, learning, knowing, along with persevering effort—together with these five, that which is excellent is a minister.
ai.translation: An excellent minister is one who possesses these five qualities: firmness of mind, protection of the citizens, learning, practical wisdom, and persevering effort.
ai.modern: மனஉறுதி, குடிகளைக் காத்தல், நூல்களைக் கற்றல், அறிவுடைமை, விடாமுயற்சி ஆகிய இந்த ஐந்து பண்புகளையும் ஒருங்கே சிறப்பாகக் கொண்டிருப்பவரே அமைச்சர் ஆவார்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the five essential qualities of an ideal minister. The first is 'vaṉkaṇ' (firmness of mind or courage), which is crucial for making tough decisions. The second is 'kuṭi kāttal' (protecting the citizens), ensuring the welfare of the people. The third and fourth are 'kaṟṟu' (learning) and 'ariṯal' (knowing/understanding), which represent theoretical education and its practical, wise application. The fifth is 'āḷviṉai' (persevering effort), without which no plan can succeed. A person who excels in all these five together is fit to be a minister.

ai.literal: And separating (enemies), cherishing and securing (allies), and reuniting those who separated, is that which a ministry is capable of.
ai.translation: A minister is one who is capable of dividing enemies, cherishing and securing allies, and winning back those who have parted ways.
ai.modern: பகைவர்களைப் பிரிப்பதும், தன் பக்கமுள்ளவர்களைப் பேணிக் காத்துக் கொள்வதும், பிரிந்து சென்றவர்களை மீண்டும் சேர்த்துக் கொள்வதும் செய்ய வல்லவரே அமைச்சர் ஆவார்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the core diplomatic duties of an able minister. First, a minister must know how to divide the allies of enemies (pirittal) to weaken them. Second, they must cherish and secure their own allies (pēṇik koḷal) to maintain strength. Third, they must be skilled at reconciling and bringing back those who have previously separated or defected (pirintārp poruttal). A true ministry is defined by the capability to perform these three strategic actions.

ai.literal: And discerning, having chosen, and executing, and decisively declaring, that which is capable of [these] is the minister.
ai.translation: A minister is one who is capable of discerning options, choosing the best course to execute, and declaring it with absolute certainty.
ai.modern: ஒரு செயலை ஆராய்ந்து அறிதலும், அவ்வாறு ஆராய்ந்த பின் சிறந்ததை முடிவு செய்து செய்தலும், அதனைத் துணிவாக எடுத்துச் சொல்லுதலும் வல்லவரே அமைச்சர் ஆவார்.
ai.explanation: This couplet outlines the three essential duties of an ideal minister. First, they must thoroughly analyze and understand a situation or problem (தெரிதல்). Second, after careful deliberation, they must choose the right course of action and execute it successfully (தேர்ந்து செயல்). Finally, they must possess the communication skills to present and defend their decisions with absolute clarity and conviction (ஒருதலையாச் சொல்லல்). Anyone who is capable of performing these three tasks effectively is fit to be a minister.

ai.literal: Knowing virtue, possessing mature and dignified speech, at all times, he who knows the best way is the companion of deliberation.
ai.translation: He who knows virtue, speaks with mature and refined words, and knows the best way to accomplish tasks, is the ultimate companion for counsel at all times.
ai.modern: அறத்தை அறிந்து, நிறைந்த பண்புகளுடன் கூடிய சொற்களைப் பேசும் ஆற்றல் உடையவனாய், எக்காலத்திலும் செயல்படும் திறனை அறிந்தவனே ஆராய்ந்து முடிவெடுப்பதற்குச் சிறந்த துணையாவான்.
ai.explanation: This couplet outlines the three essential qualities of an ideal advisor or minister. First, they must have a deep understanding of righteousness (அறனறிந்து) to ensure all decisions are ethical. Second, they must possess mature, refined, and persuasive speech (ஆன்றமைந்த சொல்லான்) to communicate counsel effectively. Third, they must have practical knowledge of the best methods to execute tasks (திறனறிந்தான்). A person with these traits is the perfect companion for deliberation (தேர்ச்சித் துணை) at all times.

ai.literal: Natural sharpness of intellect along with book-learning to those who possess, exceedingly subtle obstacles what are there before them to stand?
ai.translation: For those who possess natural sharpness of intellect along with deep learning, what obstacles are so exceedingly subtle that they can stand before them?
ai.modern: இயற்கையான அறிவு நுட்பத்தையும் அதனோடு நூல் அறிவையும் உடையவர்களுக்கு, அவர்களுக்கு முன்னால் வந்து எதிர்க்கக்கூடிய மிக நுட்பமான சூழ்ச்சிகள் அல்லது தடைகள் எவை உள்ளன?
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the supreme capability of an ideal minister who combines natural intelligence with acquired learning. The term 'mati-nuṭpam' refers to innate, sharp intellect, while 'nūlōṭu' emphasizes that this must be paired with the study of authoritative treatises. For a person endowed with both, the poet asks rhetorically what 'ati-nuṭpam' (exceedingly subtle or complex obstacles) could possibly stand in their way. Their combined wisdom easily penetrates and resolves even the most intricate challenges.

ai.literal: Theoretical knowledge even if known, the world's practical nature having understood, act.
ai.translation: Even if you have thoroughly mastered the theoretical methods of performing a task, you must understand the practical ways of the world and act accordingly.
ai.modern: ஒரு செயலைச் செய்யும் முறைகளை நூலறிவால் அறிந்திருந்தாலும், உலக நடைமுறையை அறிந்து அதற்கேற்பச் செய்ய வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the difference between theoretical knowledge and practical wisdom. The word 'செயற்கை' refers to artificial or bookish knowledge, which details the technical steps of a task. Even if a person has mastered these theories ('அறிந்தக் கடைத்தும்'), they cannot succeed without understanding 'உலகத்து இயற்கை', which refers to the natural, practical ways of the world and human behavior. A wise minister or leader must harmonize bookish rules with real-world conditions before taking action.

ai.literal: Even if [the king] is one who does not know, having destroyed [his own] intellect, speaking beneficial advice is the duty of the one who is by his side.
ai.translation: Even if the ruler has destroyed his own intellect and remains ignorant, it is the duty of the minister who stands by his side to offer sound, beneficial counsel.
ai.modern: தன் அறிவை அழித்துக் கொண்டு ஒருவன் (அரசன்) நல்லவற்றை அறியாதவனாக இருந்தாலும், அவனது அருகில் இருக்கும் அமைச்சர் அவனுக்கு நன்மையான உறுதிமொழிகளைக் கூறுவது கடமையாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet outlines the absolute duty of a minister or close advisor when dealing with an incompetent or stubborn leader. The phrase 'அறி கொன்று அறியான்' refers to a ruler who has ruined his own capacity to think and remains ignorant of what is right. The word 'எனினும்' (even if) emphasizes that the leader's ignorance is no excuse for the advisor's silence. The minister, referred to as 'உழையிருந்தான்' (the one who is by his side), must speak 'உறுதி' (firm, beneficial advice). The poet declares this to be an absolute 'கடன்' (duty), meaning the minister must perform it regardless of whether the ruler listens or gets angry.

ai.literal: Than a minister who plots ruin, seventy crore enemies by one's side are better.
ai.translation: Seventy crore open enemies by one's side are far better than a single minister who secretly plots one's ruin.
ai.modern: கேடு விளைவிக்க நினைக்கும் அமைச்சரை விட, பக்கத்தில் இருக்கும் எழுபது கோடி பகைவர்கள் மேலானவர்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns of the extreme danger posed by a treacherous minister. The word 'பழுது' means ruin or harm, and 'எண்ணும்' means plotting, describing a minister who secretly works against the ruler. The poet states that having seventy crore ('எழுபது கோடி') open enemies ('தெவ்') right next to oneself is actually preferable ('உறும்') to having one such traitor in the cabinet. An open enemy's hostility is visible and can be defended against, whereas an internal traitor destroys the state from within.

ai.literal: Even after planning methodically, only endless (unsuccessful) things will they do, those who lack capability.
ai.translation: Those who lack capability will only produce unsuccessful results, even if they have planned their actions methodically.
ai.modern: செயல்பாட்டுத் திறன் இல்லாதவர்கள், முறையோடு திட்டமிட்டாலும் கூட, வெற்றியில் முடியாத செயல்களையே செய்வார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes that planning is futile without the practical capability to execute. Even if those who lack competence (tiraṟpāṭu ilāatavar) plan their actions methodically and systematically, their endeavors will still end in failure without reaching a successful completion. The word 'tiraṟpāṭu' refers to the inherent skill or capability required to turn plans into reality. Thus, the author shows that execution capability is just as vital as strategic planning.
